_comment: Steers scripts/discover-problems.js. The agent hunts for expensive, recurring, measurable Canadian operational problems that are poorly served by current software, have usable data, and where Problem Found could build an MVP fast and get paid a cut of the savings. Edit the sectors/angles to point the hunt; the agent is told to prefer big B2B/government/industrial workflows over consumer apps.
geography: Canada (favour Ontario / GTA and other major metros, but national B2B/industrial problems are welcome)
business_model: Problem Found walks into an organisation, shows it is losing a large, measurable amount of money on a specific manual or underserved workflow, and offers to build the software that fixes it in exchange for a cut of the savings (a fee in the ~$50k–$300k range that is a fraction of what the organisation saves in year one). We only want problems where that pitch is credible.
must_have: Expensive: a single organisation plausibly loses six or seven figures per year (CAD) to this problem.
Recurring: the pain repeats daily/weekly/monthly or every project, not a one-off.
Measurable: there is a concrete metric (hours, dollars, error rate, downtime, penalties) we could move and show.
Underserved by software: no dominant off-the-shelf tool already solves it well for this segment.
Usable data exists: the inputs needed to build a demo are public, purchasable, or already sitting in the customer's systems.
Identifiable buyer: a role that owns both the budget and the pain.
Demoable: we could build a convincing MVP with synthetic or public data in days, not months.
Repeatable: many similar Canadian organisations share the same problem.
avoid: Consumer apps and anything depending on viral growth or advertising.
Problems requiring a large proprietary data moat, hardware, or heavy regulatory approval before any value.
Generic 'add AI to X' with no specific expensive workflow.
Pure research problems with no organisation that would pay to have them solved.
Markets dominated by an entrenched, well-loved incumbent tool.
sectors: Construction, developers, general contractors and infrastructure owners
Municipal and provincial government operations and permitting
Utilities, energy, power reliability and field service
Logistics, trucking, warehousing and cold chain
Healthcare operations, clinics, long-term care and diagnostics scheduling
Manufacturing, food processing and industrial maintenance
Legal, accounting, compliance and professional services back-office
Real estate, property management and facilities
Mining, forestry, agriculture and natural resources
Legacy enterprise systems, mainframe operations and mission-critical back-office workflows
angles: Manual spreadsheet workflows that quietly cost a team days every week
Penalties, fines, liquidated damages or clawbacks caused by missed deadlines or bad paperwork
Reconciliation between systems that never talk to each other
Expensive expert time spent on work a system could pre-assemble
Dispatch, scheduling and routing decisions made by gut feel
Evidence, audit and claim reconstruction done from scattered documents
Waste, downtime, spoilage or unnecessary truck-rolls that data could prevent
Compliance reporting assembled by hand under deadline
Critical workflows constrained by scarce mainframe, COBOL, industrial-control or domain specialists whose preparatory work and decision evidence could be captured
